newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia spends $2.2 mln on public relations - report.
newsitem.headline: Colombia spends $2.2 mln on public relations - report.

text.p: Colombia has spent $2.2 million to improve its public image in the lead-up to a U.S. decision on whether to "certify" the country as an ally in the fight against drugs, a leading daily said on Sunday.

The El Tiempo newspaper said President Ernesto Samper's government had contracts with four public relations firms to lobby the U.S. Congress and put together a media advertising campaign to highlight the advances Colombia has made in the fight to stem cocaine and heroin trafficking in the last year.
U.S. President Bill Clinton blacklisted Colombia last March for its perceived failure to crack down hard enough on drug trafficking.

Colombian officials believe it is likely the country will be decertified for a second consecutive year and fear the United States could also impose economic sanctions. The decision is due to be announced on Feb. 27.

According to El Tiempo, under terms of one of the contracts worth $1.7 million, the Miami-based Kelly Swofford agency takes on the task of "influencing U.S. policies and perceptions of Colombia's anti-drug efforts with the ultimate aim of overturning (last year's) decertification decision."

But senior U.S. anti-drug officials remain highly critical of Colombia's track record despite the recent approval of a tough new law to strip drug kingpins of their ill-gotten gains and legislation that would almost triple the maximum jail term for drug-related crimes.
